title: // SAFETY: comment on non-unsafe .unwrap() is misleading
description: lifecycle.rs line ~1088 uses '// SAFETY: system clock is always after UNIX_EPOCH' before a .unwrap() call. SAFETY: is a Rust convention specifically for unsafe blocks — it names the invariant that makes the unsafe code sound. Using it on a safe .unwrap() is misleading: readers and tools like cargo-geiger associate SAFETY comments with unsafe. The correct marker for a documented safe unwrap is a plain comment, e.g. '// Cannot fail: system clock is always after UNIX_EPOCH on any supported platform'. Same correction needed in server_stores.rs once issue sp5s.4 is applied.
